body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.
body.ar: قيود المجال والدالة العكسية: تمتلك الدالة \(f\) معكوساً \(f^{-1}\) إذا وفقط إذا كانت متباينة (واحد لواحد)، ويكون مجال \(f^{-1}\) هو مدى \(f\) تماماً.

body.en:
1. Exponential Relationship \( y = ab^x \):
Take natural logs of both sides: \( \ln y = \ln(a \cdot b^x) = \ln a + x \ln b \).
In \( Y = mX + c \) form: \( Y = \ln y \), \( X = x \), gradient \( m = \ln b \implies b = e^m \), and intercept \( c = \ln a \implies a = e^c \).

2. Power Relationship \( y = Ax^n \):
\( \ln y = \ln A + n \ln x \).
Here: \( Y = \ln y \), \( X = \ln x \), gradient \( m = n \), and intercept \( c = \ln A \implies A = e^c \).

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).
body.ar: برهان إكمال المربع وتحديد المدى: بكتابة \(ax^2+bx+c = a(x+\frac{b}{2a})^2 + (c-\frac{b^2}{4a})\) وبما أن المربع الكامل غير سالب دائماً، يتحدد رأس القطع ومدى الدالة بدقة.

label.en: Worked Example 3.A — Linear Law Model Fitting

body.en:
Variables \( x \) and \( y \) are related by \( y = ab^x \). A plot of \( \ln y \) against \( x \) produces a straight line passing through \( (2, 3.4) \) and \( (6, 5.8) \). Find the values of \( a \) and \( b \) to 3 significant figures.

Solution:
Gradient \( m = \frac{5.8 - 3.4}{6 - 2} = \frac{2.4}{4} = 0.6 \).
Since \( m = \ln b \implies \ln b = 0.6 \implies b = e^{0.6} \approx 1.82 \).
Equation of line: \( Y - 3.4 = 0.6(X - 2) \implies Y = 0.6X + 2.2 \).
The vertical intercept is \( c = 2.2 \).
Since \( c = \ln a \implies a = e^{2.2} \approx 9.03 \).
Answer: \( a \approx 9.03, \, b \approx 1.82 \).

body.en:
Problem (Hard): The polynomial identity \( (6x + 1)(x + 10) = 6x^2 + fx + 10 \) holds for all \( x \). Find the linear coefficient \( f \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Expanding the product gives \( f = 6\cdot 10 + 1 = 61 \).

Problem (Easy): The graph of the quadratic function \( f(x) = (x - 5)(x + 8) \) intersects the horizontal axis at two points. Find the distance \( d_{AB} \) between the two intercepts of \( f(x) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The intercepts are at \( 5 \) and \( -8 \), separated by distance \( 5 - (-8) = 13 \).

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Logarithms, Exponentials & Straight-Line Reduction (Medium Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول D — اللوغاريتمات والدوال الأسية والتحويل للخط المستقيم (تطبيق Medium)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): Solve the simultaneous system: \( \log_2(x) - \log_2(y) = 2 \) and \( x - 3y = 3 \). What is the value of \( x \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: From the first equation: \( \log_2(x/y) = 2 \implies x/y = 2^2 = 4 \implies x = 4y \). Substitute into second: \( 4y - 3y = 3 \implies y = 3 \). Thus \( x = 4(3) = 12 \).

body.en:
1. Extraneous Roots in Logarithmic & Radical Equations: On Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics (0606), solving \(\log_2(x) + \log_2(x - 3) = 6\) or \(\sqrt{x + 6} = x - 1\) produces two quadratic roots, one of which makes the original log argument \(\le 0\) or the RHS of the square root negative. Failing to reject the extraneous root costs the final accuracy mark.

2. Confusing Removable Holes with Vertical Asymptotes: If \((x - 3)\) cancels from both numerator and denominator of \(R(x)\), then \(x = 3\) is a removable hole (point discontinuity), not a vertical asymptote.

body.en: Fast Exam Check (Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics (0606)): To verify an inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) in 5 seconds, pick a simple input \(x_0\), compute \(y_0 = f(x_0)\), and check that \(f^{-1}(y_0) = x_0\). Also verify that the graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) reflects \(y = f(x)\) across \(y = x\).
